Parked and Forgotten: 1969 Daimler Sovereign Is Wasting Away in Very Old Barn
8 photos
Photo: IMSTOKZE/YouTube
When it comes to barn-found classics, I love the stories in which the vehicles get rescued and revived . Sadly, these stories aren't very common. Most barn finds never get a second chance and end up wasting away. This old British sedan is one of those rigs.
We're looking at a Daimler Sovereign, which is an iconic part of British automotive history. Although it may not be particularly famous outside the UK, Daimler is a big name on the island, particularly for having supplied cars to the royal family from 1902 until the 1950s.
Purchased by the Birmingham Small Arms Company in 1910, Daimler became a part of Jaguar in 1960. The latter began using the name on upscale versions of its cars. In 1968, Daimler got a standalone model called the DS420, which became an official state car in many countries.
This Daimler is a Sovereign, which debuted in 1966 as a more luxurious version of the Jaguar 420 sedan, which in turn was based on the S-Type. In 1969, the Sovereign name was transferred to the brand-new XJ6 architecture. The car you see here is a first-year model, and, according to the owner, it's also one of the first examples ever made.
Unfortunately, this Daimler spent a lot of time in a very old barn. The owner reportedly bought it for restoration. The car was still running and driving at the time it was parked. But as is often the case, life got in the way, and the owner never got around to start the restoration.
It's unclear when it was parked, but it must have been sitting for decades. The blue paint is heavily weathered, while the interior sustained notable damage due to prolonged exposure to moisture. The original engine is still under the hood, but it looks like it will need a rebuild to fire up again.
By the way, the XJ6 it is based on was offered with Jaguar's iconic XK inline-six engine. Owners could choose between the 2.8 or 4.2-liter version. The former came with 104 horsepower on tap, while the latter delivered 246 horsepower. The XJ6 and Sovereign were the last Jaguars powered by the XK engine.
The owner says he is now too old to take care of the car, and it's unclear whether he wants to sell it or not. Whatever the case, this Daimler needs a new home ASAP because it's pretty close to the point where it's no longer worth restoring.
These cars aren't particularly valuable, though. They rarely fetch over $30,000 at public auctions, with most examples having sold for well under $20,000 in recent years. All told, the restoration would have to be a labor of love . Hit the play button below to check it out. The Dailmer footage starts at the 16-minute mark.
